<thought>Based on the observed mass spectrum, the base peak at m/z 194.086 likely corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 193.079 Da. The strong M+2 peak (~33 % of the base) is characteristic of a single chlorine atom (⁷⁵Cl/⁷⁷Cl isotopic pattern). A formula that matches the neutral mass and includes one chlorine is C₉H₁₈O₂Cl (monoisotopic mass 193.099 Da, within experimental error). This formula also predicts an M+1 intensity (~10 % from ¹³C plus minor contributions) consistent with the observed 13 % M+1 peak. Therefore, the molecular formula is C9H18O2Cl.</thought>
<final_answer>C9H18O2Cl</final_answer>
